short: Hand-pressed fingertip EMG (M05) is standard: privacy and noise benefits argued, not tested; 97.2% on 30 words rests on a random within-participant split with no session hold-out (M12, behind).
position: The paper [@kurotaki2026softemg] changes one component, the sensor (M05): dry electrodes on four fingertips (one channel each) of a hand-worn soft package, pressed to the perioral skin only during input. Earlier neck- and ear-worn dry electrodes [@wu2024necklace; @tang2025headphones] also avoid facial adhesives, and the claimed privacy and noise benefits are argued, not measured, so M05 is standard. The evaluation (M12) is behind the best comparable work: the 97.2% headline comes from a random class-stratified split within each participant, while worn sEMG systems tested on a held-out session lose 14 to 23 points on 8-word tasks [@meier2025neckband; @spacone2026silentwear]. The authors concede that hand pressing adds placement variability (§ Discussion), so the missing session-disjoint test is the strongest confound. Deployment (M13) is standard: PC decoding with no latency, power or command success figure.
